title: Living Room Negative Space
description: How to allocate negative space reasonably to create an open, spacious feeling for Southeast Asian style living rooms.
content:
Modern Southeast Asian style places special emphasis on the proportion of negative space in interior design. An airy space not only creates a sense of spaciousness but also promotes better air circulation — something extremely important in Vietnam's tropical humid climate.

## The 60-30-10 Rule

A golden rule in Southeast Asian style design is to allocate space according to the 60-30-10 ratio: 60% of the area left empty or for circulation, 30% for main furniture, and 10% for decorations.

## Natural Materials for an Airy Feel

Using light-toned natural wood, rattan weaving, and linen fabric are popular choices. These materials are not only environmentally friendly but also create a light, unheavy feeling for the space.

## Natural Light

Making the most of natural light is key. Large windows, white sheer curtains, and avoiding tall furniture that blocks light will help the living room become brighter and more spacious.

## Indoor Plants

Placing 2-3 potted plants in room corners or on wall-mounted shelves not only creates visual focal points but also makes the space more lively. Plants like money tree, snake plant, or pothos are all suitable for indoor conditions in Vietnam.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: French Vietnamese Style vs European French
description: Comparing the differences between French style in Vietnam and Europe, from colors to decorative details.
content:
French Colonial (Indochine) style in Vietnam is a unique combination of French architectural elegance and Indochinese cultural identity. However, it differs significantly from typical French style in Europe.

## Colors: From Cool to Warm

While European French interiors typically use cool neutral tones like gray, pure white combined with navy blue or black accents, French Vietnamese style favors warm tones like cream, beige, light turquoise, and earth yellow.

## Materials: Climate Adaptation

French architecture in Europe often uses natural stone, heavy oak, and fireplaces. In Vietnam, Indochine designs have adapted by using moisture-resistant teak wood, white marble, and cement tiles to create a cool feeling.

## Decorative Details

Arched doorways, wrought iron railings, and crystal chandeliers are common elements. However, in Vietnam, we often see combinations with rattan weaving, Vietnamese silk paintings, and Bat Trang ceramics — features that cannot be found in original French design.

## Open Spaces

French-style townhouses in Vietnam usually have a courtyard or small balcony — elements rarely seen in typical French architecture but very suitable for the tropical climate.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Southeast Asian Humidity-Resistant Materials
description: Choosing materials suitable for tropical humid climates, from natural wood to artificial stone.
content:
Vietnam's tropical humid climate, with average humidity of 70-80% and long rainy seasons, poses significant challenges for choosing interior materials. Here are the optimal choices proven over time.

## Natural Wood: Teak and Cam Xe

Teak wood is highly regarded for its natural moisture resistance and termite resistance. The natural oils in teak create a protective layer that makes water difficult to penetrate. Cam xe wood is a more economical choice, equally sturdy and durable.

## Artificial Stone (Quartz)

Instead of natural stone that easily absorbs water and stains, artificial quartz is an ideal solution for kitchen countertops and dining tables. Non-porous, easy to clean, and highly durable.

## Anti-Humidity Interior Paint

Use paint with anti-humidity components, especially for north-facing walls and low-lying areas. Dulux Weathershield and Jotun Majestic are two paint lines trusted by many Vietnamese families.

## Fabrics and Leather

Linen and cotton fabrics are the best choices for sofas and curtains because they are breathable and quick-drying. Stay away from synthetic leather (PU) because it easily peels in humid environments. Genuine leather or microfiber fabric are better alternatives.

## Ventilation Blocks

As a characteristic of Vietnamese architecture, ventilation blocks are not only decorative elements but also help air circulation, naturally reducing indoor humidity.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: How to Choose Cream Paint
description: Guide to selecting the right cream color paint to create a warm and elegant space.
content:
Cream is one of the most beloved colors in French Colonial and modern minimalist interior design. However, choosing the right cream shade is not always easy.

## Popular Cream Tones

- **Cool cream:** Has a hint of gray or blue, suitable for rooms with abundant natural light.
- **Warm cream:** Has a hint of yellow or orange, creating a cozy feeling for rooms lacking light.
- **Ivory:** Closer to white, creating a clean and spacious feeling.

## Combining with Other Colors

Cream walls paired with dark wood (walnut) create an elegant contrast. If you prefer a softer style, combine with light-colored wood (oak, ash) and turquoise or light green accessories.

## Testing Paint Before Painting

Always test paint samples on real walls and observe under different lighting conditions (early morning, noon, evening). Paint color can change significantly depending on house orientation and light source.

## Paint Finishes

- **Matte:** Good at hiding wall imperfections, creates a luxurious feeling but is difficult to clean.
- **Eggshell/Satin:** Balances aesthetics and durability, suitable for living rooms and bedrooms.
- **Semi-gloss:** Easy to clean, suitable for kitchens and bathrooms.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: 5 Tips to Turn a Small Apartment into a Resort
description: Transform your small apartment into a resort-like space with 5 simple tips.
content:
You don't need a beachfront villa to have a resort feeling. With these 5 tips, your small apartment can also become a private resort.

## 1. Maximize Natural Light

Replace heavy curtains with thin white or beige linen curtains. Natural light is the most important factor in creating that airy resort feeling.

## 2. Add Plants

Just 3-5 potted plants placed in room corners are enough to create a sense of closeness to nature. Pothos, money tree, or snake plant are all easy to care for.

## 3. Use Natural Materials

Replace synthetic fabric cushion covers with linen or cotton pillowcases. Straw rugs, bamboo blinds, and natural wood products all contribute to creating a relaxing feeling.

## 4. Create a Meditation Corner

Set aside a small corner (just 1 square meter) with a comfortable chair, a warm yellow lamp, and perhaps a landscape painting. This will be your place to relax after a long workday.

## 5. Scents

A bottle of lemongrass, lavender, or grapefruit essential oil in the living room will immediately create a spa-like feeling. Scented candles are also a wonderful choice for the evening.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Budget-Friendly Arched Doorways
description: Affordable alternatives to traditional arched doorways.
content:
Arched doorways are a symbol of French Colonial style, but building a real arch requires high costs and technical skill. Here are budget-friendly alternatives that still maintain classical beauty.

## Solution 1: Plaster Fake Arch

Instead of building an arch with bricks, you can frame a plasterboard arch above a regular doorway. Costs are reduced by 70% but the visual effect is similar.

## Solution 2: Arched Shelves

Create a recessed arched shelf in the living room or bedroom. This is a very economical way to bring the arch element into your living space without touching the structure.

## Solution 3: Arched Mirror

A large mirror with an arched frame hung on the wall not only creates a style focal point but also helps the space look larger.

## Solution 4: Arched Window

If you're renovating, consider replacing a square window with an arched window. Much easier to construct than an arched doorway because it doesn't bear weight.

## Colors and Finishes

Arched doorways should be painted white or cream to create an airy feeling. If you want to create a focal point, you can expose brick edges or natural stone around the arch.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: 5 Million VND Budget Decorating Guide
description: Decorate your home beautifully with a budget of just 5 million VND.
content:
You don't need to spend too much to have a beautiful and comfortable living space. With a budget of 5 million VND, here is the most efficient allocation.

## 1. Fresh Wall Paint (1.5 million)

A new coat of paint can completely change the appearance of a room. Choose white or cream to create a spacious feeling. Painting yourself can save 50% of labor costs.

## 2. Curtains (800k)

Linen or cotton curtains in white/beige from affordable home stores. Avoid buying expensive ready-made curtains; buy fabric and have them custom-made instead.

## 3. Decorative Lighting (700k)

A beautifully designed floor lamp or table lamp as a focal point. Shopee and secondhand markets have many reasonably priced options.

## 4. Plants and Pots (500k)

3-4 potted plants of various types combined with simple ceramic pots. Pothos, money tree, and succulents are all easy to keep alive and affordable.

## 5. Cushions and Rug (1 million)

Cushion covers with simple patterns and a small rug under the coffee table. These details immediately create a cozy feeling.

## 6. Small Decorations (500k)

Photo frames, scented candles, or a ceramic vase. These small details reflect the homeowner's personality.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: 10 Common Decorating Mistakes in Vietnam
description: Common mistakes when decorating homes in Vietnam and how to fix them.
content:
After years of observation and consultation, we notice some home decorating mistakes repeating in many Vietnamese families. Here are the 10 most common mistakes and how to fix them.

## 1. Lighting Too Cool or Too Yellow

Many families use 6500K LED lights (cool white) throughout the house, creating a hospital-like feeling. Solution: Use 3000K (warm yellow) for bedrooms and 4000K (neutral) for living rooms.

## 2. Curtains Too Short

Curtains only cover to the window, exposing the frame. Solution: Hang curtains 15-20cm higher than the window and let them touch the floor to create a higher ceiling feeling.

## 3. Too Many Small Decorative Items

Bookshelves packed with small souvenirs create a cluttered feeling. Solution: Apply the 'less is more' rule — only keep items that truly have meaning.

## 4. Rug Too Small

The rug only fits under the coffee table, not reaching the sofa legs. Solution: The rug must be large enough for the front legs of the sofa/chairs to rest on it.

## 5. All Furniture from the Same Set

Buying a complete set of sofa, table, and cabinet from one store creates a showroom feeling. Solution: Mix items from various sources to create unique personality.

## 6. Ignoring Natural Light

Hanging thick black curtains or placing tall cabinets blocking windows. Solution: Make the most of natural light, use sheer curtains or bamboo blinds.

## 7. No Color Accents

The entire house in one white or beige color is boring. Solution: Choose an accent color (turquoise, earth orange, or green) for cushions, paintings, or an accent chair.

## 8. Furniture Not Matching Proportions

Sofa too large for a small living room or dining table too small for a spacious area. Solution: Measure carefully before buying, draw a layout diagram.

## 9. Ignoring Wall Space

Empty walls create an unwelcoming feeling. Solution: Hang 1-2 large paintings or a set of small paintings (gallery wall).

## 10. No Plants

Space lacks vitality. Solution: Just 2-3 easy-to-care-for plants are enough to change the atmosphere.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: 10 Common Tile Selection Mistakes
description: Frequent mistakes when choosing tiles for homes in Vietnam and how to avoid them.
content:
## 1. Choosing Overly Glossy Tiles for Wet Areas
Glossy tiles become extremely slippery when wet, particularly dangerous in bathrooms and kitchen areas. Choose tiles with a rough surface or anti-slip tiles with a high friction coefficient for these areas.

## 2. Using Tiles Too Small for Large Spaces
Small tiles (30x30cm) in a spacious living room create a cluttered feel with too many grout lines. Choose large-format tiles (60x60cm or 80x80cm) for open spaces to create a more seamless and luxurious effect.

## 3. Ignoring Anti-Slip Ratings
Many people focus only on color and pattern, forgetting to check slip resistance ratings (R9, R10, R11). Bathrooms, terraces, and outdoor areas need tiles with at least R10 slip resistance.

## 4. Not Considering Color and Pattern
Choosing tiles too dark makes the room feel dim and cramped. Stone-vein or wood-grain tiles must be carefully checked for pattern repetition — too much repetition looks artificial and less premium.

## 5. Choosing Low-Quality Tiles to Save Costs
Cheap tiles often have high water absorption, easily staining and cracking after a period of use. Investing in quality tiles from the start saves more than replacing them after 2-3 years.

## 6. Using Too Many Polished Tiles in the Living Room
Polished tiles strongly reflect light, causing glare and an unpleasant 'ice rink' effect. Instead, consider matte tiles, honed tiles, or stone-vein tiles with a natural surface.

## 7. Not Calculating Tile Size vs Room Proportions
60x120cm elongated tiles can make a small room appear longer but also narrower. Calculate tile direction and room proportions before deciding on tile size for the best visual effect.

## 8. Ignoring Water and Stain Resistance
Glossy glazed tiles have better water resistance than unglazed matte tiles. For kitchen and bathroom areas, choose tiles with water absorption below 0.5% and surface stain treatment for easy cleaning.

## 9. Not Coordinating Wall and Floor Tiles
Mismatched wall and floor tiles create a disharmonious and patchwork feel. Choose wall and floor tiles in the same color tone or from the same collection to ensure spatial consistency.

## 10. Buying Tiles Without Checking the Actual Batch
Tile colors can vary between different production batches. Always request to see actual products, check batch numbers, and purchase 10-15% extra for future replacements.

Conclusion: Choosing tiles seems simple but hides many pitfalls that first-time buyers can fall into. Hopefully, the 10 common mistakes analyzed above will give you a clearer perspective and help you make wise decisions for your home. Always remember: investing correctly from the start saves many times over compared to future repairs.
author: NhàXinh Team

title: Beautiful Home Decor on a Budget Under 10 Million VND
description: Transform your home into a beautiful space without spending too much money.
content:
## 1. Use Accent Paint
Instead of painting all walls, choose one accent wall with bold colors like emerald, earth orange, or moss green. Cost is only about 300-500 thousand VND but the space transformation is significant.

## 2. Change the Curtains
Old curtains can completely change a room's appearance. With a budget of 500-800 thousand VND, you can sew linen or cotton cream-colored curtains for a more airy and modern feel.

## 3. Buy Second-Hand Furniture
Flea markets, Facebook groups, or clearance furniture shops are treasures for limited budgets. A wooden coffee table, bookshelf, or good-condition sofa can be purchased at just 30-40% of the new price.

## 4. Add Plants
Plants are the cheapest way to refresh a space. Spend 300-500 thousand VND on 3-4 plants like pothos, money tree, or succulents with simple ceramic pots to instantly bring life to a room.

## 5. Use Decorative Lighting
A well-designed floor lamp or table lamp with warm yellow light creates a focal point and cozy atmosphere. Shopee has many decorative lighting options from just 200-400 thousand VND.

## 6. Repurpose Old Items
Repainting old wardrobes, replacing cabinet handles, or turning old wooden crates into coffee tables are smart recycling methods. A small can of paint and a new set of handles cost only about 200 thousand VND but deliver surprising results.

## 7. Cushions and Rugs
Replace cushion covers with new colors and add a small rug under the coffee table. With 500-700 thousand VND, you can buy 3-4 cushion covers and a small wool rug, instantly creating coziness.

## 8. Wall Decor with Photos
Print family photos or buy affordable canvas art to create a gallery wall on empty walls. Cost is only 200-400 thousand VND for 3-5 frames, turning blank walls into artistic focal points.

## 9. Rearrange Furniture
Sometimes you don't need to buy anything — just changing the position of the sofa, shelves, and coffee table gives the room a completely new look. Try different layouts before deciding to buy new furniture.

Conclusion: Decorating your home on a budget under 10 million VND is entirely feasible if you prioritize and get creative. Start with the smallest changes, and gradually perfect your living space in your own way.
author: NhàXinh Team

title: Minimalist Bedroom Design - The Ideal Rest Space
description: Tips for designing a modern minimalist bedroom for better sleep and a relaxed mind.
content:
The bedroom is the most important private space in the home, where you recharge after a long day. Minimalist style with its 'less is more' philosophy is particularly suited for bedrooms, as a tidy, airy space helps the mind relax and fall asleep more easily.

## Core Principles of a Minimalist Bedroom

A minimalist bedroom doesn't mean empty and lifeless. Rather, it focuses on truly essential items with high practical value. Start by removing unnecessary things: a desk in the bedroom, overloaded bookshelves, or scattered decorations. **Every item in a minimalist bedroom must have a clear purpose.**

## Color Palette and Materials

The minimalist bedroom color palette revolves around neutral tones: cream white, beige, light gray, and earth brown. These colors create a quiet foundation that rests the eyes. Main materials should be **light-toned natural wood** (oak, ash) combined with linen, cotton, and wool fabrics. Avoid using too many glossy surfaces as they reflect light and create unnecessary luxury.

## The Bed - Focal Point of the Space

The bed is the most important piece. Choose a bed with a simple design, no elaborate headboard, or a flat upholstered headboard. **White or beige bedding sets** in Egyptian cotton or premium linen. Just 2-3 cushions instead of the pile of pillows you'd see in showrooms.

## Light and Space

Maximize natural light with white sheer curtains. In the evening, use **warm yellow bedside lamps (2700-3000K)** instead of harsh ceiling lights. A small floor lamp in the corner also creates a cozy atmosphere. Keep at least 60% of the floor space clear to let the space 'breathe'.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Scandinavian Bedroom - Warm and Serene in the Tropics
description: Bring Scandinavian breath into Vietnamese bedrooms with light tones, natural wood, and cozy hygge details.
content:
Scandinavian style is renowned for its elegant, minimalist yet warm beauty. Contrary to popular belief, this style can be successfully applied in Vietnam's tropical climate, even creating a cooler, more airy feeling.

## Nordic Colors in a Tropical Bedroom

Scandinavian style primarily uses white as a base, combined with light gray, beige, and pastel tones. In Vietnam, you can replace cool white with **warm white** to better suit the golden southern light. Color accents come from small accessories: mint green cushions, mustard wool blankets, or a nature-print painting.

## Light-Toned Wood - The Soul of Scandinavia

**Oak** and **ash** with natural light tones are the top choices. Beds, wardrobes, and vanities should have clean lines and raised legs for a light feel and easy cleaning. On a limited budget, you can repaint old furniture white or beige for the same effect.

## Hygge - The Secret to Coziness

Hygge (pronounced 'hu-guh') is the Danish concept of coziness and comfort. In a Nordic bedroom, hygge is expressed through: **thick wool rugs**, warm lamps with fabric shades, soft cashmere blankets, and scented candles. A small reading nook by the window with a comfy armchair and reading lamp is also a perfect hygge touch.

## Plants in the Nordic Bedroom

Scandinavians love nature, so plants are essential. Place **2-3 small plants** like snake plants, money trees, or succulents on the windowsill or wall-mounted shelves. White or terracotta pots best suit this style.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Japanese-Style Compact Kitchen - Optimized Down to the Centimeter
description: Discover how to design a kitchen following Japanese philosophy: tidy, organized, and full of cooking inspiration.
content:
Japanese kitchens are renowned for their meticulous organization down to the smallest detail. For Vietnamese kitchens that are often modest in size, Japanese style offers an optimal solution: utilizing every centimeter of space while maintaining refined aesthetic beauty.

## Space Organization Principles

Japanese style emphasizes clear zone division: **prep area, cooking area, and washing area**. The kitchen triangle (stove - sink - refrigerator) is designed with reasonable distances to optimize movement. Unlike Western kitchens that often have large islands, Japanese kitchens prioritize continuous counter space and wall-mounted cabinets.

## Materials and Colors

**Dark natural wood** (walnut) combined with black/gray granite or quartz creates the characteristic deep warm palette. Kitchen walls are clad in white subway tiles or white ceramic tiles for brightness. Accents come from bamboo, rattan, or Japanese ceramic elements. **Keep the counter always clear**, leaving only truly essential tools like wooden spoons, Japanese knives, and cutting boards.

## Smart Storage Systems

The Japanese are masters of storage. In a Japanese kitchen, everything has its place: **divided drawers for knives, spoons, forks; wall cabinets with adjustable height shelves; lazy Susan corner spice racks**. Utilize the space under the sink with sliding shelves and storage baskets. Kitchen cabinets should reach the ceiling to avoid dust accumulation on top.

## Zen Elements in the Kitchen

A small tea corner with a **teapot and ceramic tea cups** is not just for brewing tea but also a restful stop during cooking sessions. A small bonsai or pothos plant on the kitchen shelf also contributes to creating a peaceful, zen-like atmosphere.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Modern Minimalist Kitchen - Less Stuff, More Convenience
description: Design a kitchen following minimalism — where every item has a purpose and the space stays airy.
content:
Modern minimalist kitchens are becoming the top interior design trend in Vietnam. More young families are choosing this style for its intelligence, easy maintenance, and ability to visually 'expand' often limited kitchen spaces.

## Seamless Cabinet Fronts

The hallmark of a minimalist kitchen is **flat, handleless cabinets**. Push-to-open or integrated handle systems create a seamless surface that's easy to wipe clean. Cabinet colors should be uniform — white, gray, or natural wood tone — avoiding multiple colors that create visual clutter. **White quartz countertops** or microcement are ideal choices.

## Integrated Appliances - The Key to Tidiness

**All appliances should be built into cabinets:** dishwasher, oven, range hood, and even the refrigerator. A built-in induction hob keeps the counter completely flat when not in use. This not only creates minimalist beauty but also makes cleaning easier than ever.

## The 'Clear Counter' Rule

**Keeping the countertop completely clear** is the biggest challenge but also the deciding factor for a successful minimalist kitchen. Coffee machines, blenders, microwaves — all should be stored in cabinets or smart cabinets with lift mechanisms. Only leave a few essentials like a small vase or a potted plant.

## Minimalist Yet Refined Lighting

Lighting in a minimalist kitchen serves to create accents. **Recessed LED strips** along cabinet areas, recessed downlights, and a geometric pendant light above the island with a simple design — that's all you need. Color temperature should be maintained at 4000K (neutral) for true-to-life light while cooking.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Elegant French Dining Room - The Art of Dining and Decor
description: Transform the dining room into a luxurious, romantic space with French architectural inspiration and Vietnamese touches.
content:
In French culture, a meal is not just refueling but an art — where the family gathers, converses, and savors every moment. A French-style dining room therefore always carries a romantic, refined, and emotional beauty.

## The Dining Table - Center of the Space

A **natural wood dining table** is the soul of a French dining room. Oak, walnut, or teak with a finely sanded surface and matte finish creates a luxurious feel. The table shape can be a classic rectangle or round for smaller spaces. **Upholstered dining chairs** with gently curved backs in cream or gray bring the characteristic French elegance.

## Chandelier - Architectural Accent

A crystal or brass chandelier is indispensable. Hang it 75-90cm above the table for focused dining light. For smaller spaces, substitute with **3-5 mini pendants** arranged in a line along the table length.

## French Table Setting

A **white or subtly striped linen tablecloth** combined with cloth napkins and brass napkin rings. White ceramic tableware with gold or light blue rims. The table always has a fresh flower vase — **roses, lavender, or white chrysanthemums** — in a ceramic or clear glass vase.

## Vietnamese Touches in a French Dining Room

To create distinction, add Vietnamese elements: **Bat Trang ceramic tea sets**, Vietnamese silk paintings on the wall, or a large ceramic vase in the corner. This combination creates a unique Indochine style, both luxurious and close to Vietnamese culture.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Southeast Asian Dining Space - Cozy and Rich in Identity
description: Design a dining room with Southeast Asian cultural spirit, natural materials, warm colors, and open space.
content:
Southeast Asian cuisine is known for its richness and bold flavors, and the dining space should reflect that spirit. Southeast Asian style in dining room design blends natural materials, warm colors, and an intimate, close-knit atmosphere.

## Large Wood Dining Table - Gathering Place

A **large teak or rosewood dining table** is the center of the Southeast Asian dining room. Natural wood surfaces, sometimes with raw grain and original color, create a rustic and authentic feel. Rectangular tables with softened rounded edges or round tables give a sense of togetherness. Rattan-woven wood chairs or simple unupholstered wood chairs are popular choices.

## Local Colors and Patterns

**The Southeast Asian dining room palette** includes warm earth tones: earth brown, earth orange, turmeric yellow, green, and brick red. Batik, ikat, or ethnic minority patterns on cushions, tablecloths, or wall hangings create unique cultural accents. However, use patterns moderately — just 1-2 accent points in the room.

## Natural and Handcrafted Materials

**Rattan, seagrass, and ceramics** are three essential materials. Rattan seat cushions replace fabric chairs in hot, humid climates. Blue-glazed or earth-brown ceramic tableware, bamboo chopsticks, and seagrass mats create an authentic Southeast Asian dining experience.

## Connection with Nature

A Southeast Asian dining room is ideal when directly connected to nature. Large windows opening to a garden or balcony, indoor plants near the dining table, and **natural ventilation systems** instead of relying entirely on air conditioning. A ventilation block wall or bamboo screen also creates a connection to nature. Warm light from lanterns or rattan lights creates a cozy atmosphere for family dinners.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Bohemian Balcony - A Green Paradise in the City
description: Transform your balcony into a Bohemian-style art garden with plants, colorful fabrics, and ethnic accessories.
content:
The balcony is the space connecting the home with the outside world. Bohemian (Boho) style, with its free-spirited essence, vibrant colors, and free mix of materials, is the perfect choice to turn a balcony into a green oasis amid the noisy city.

## Plants - The Soul of the Boho Balcony

**Plants are the most important element** in Bohemian style. Combine various plants with different heights and foliage: tall plants like areca palm, rubber plant; medium plants like pothos, ferns; small plants like succulents, cacti. Hang plants on walls, place them on shelves, and suspend them from the ceiling for a hanging garden effect. **Terracotta-colored pots** are the soul of Boho style.

## Colorful Fabrics and Patterns

**Ethnic-pattern cushions and rugs** blending Mexican, Indian, and Turkish motifs. Main colors: brick red, mustard yellow, emerald, lavender purple, and terracotta orange. A kilim rug on the floor, 3-5 cushions on a rattan or hammock chair, and **a paper lantern** or LED string lights create a romantic evening atmosphere.

## Mobile and Multi-Functional Furniture

A Boho balcony doesn't need expensive furniture. **Rattan chairs, hammocks, small folding tables, and recycled wood pallets** as seats or tables are wonderful choices. A small bookshelf or an old wooden cabinet painted in pastel colors as an accent. All furniture should be easily movable for flexible layout changes.

## Bohemian Decor Accessories

Boho accessories have no strict rules — the more personality, the better! **Wind chimes, hand-embroidered art, decorative wall masks, macrame mirrors, colorful scented candles, and hand-painted ceramic vases** are all great suggestions. Hang a small decorative tapestry on the wall as a focal point. Most importantly: choose items that make you feel happy and comfortable.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Scandinavian Study - Focus and Creativity
description: Design a home study and workspace in Scandinavian style, optimizing focus and creative inspiration.
content:
With the growing trend of remote work, a well-designed study not only boosts productivity but also protects physical and mental health. Scandinavian style, with its simplicity, functionality, and closeness to nature, is the ideal choice for this space.

## Desk and Chair - Ergonomics is Priority Number One

An **oak or pine desk** with a simple design, slim legs, or an adjustable standing desk. The desk should be at least 120cm wide for a computer, books, and personal items. The work chair **needs lumbar support** and height adjustability. In Scandinavian style, chairs typically have a slim design, mesh or fabric upholstery, prioritizing breathability.

## Lighting - The Productivity Factor

**Maximize natural light.** Place the desk parallel to the window (not facing or backing it) to avoid glare. White sheer linen curtains help diffuse soft light. In the evening, use a **desk lamp with an articulating arm** and 4000K (neutral) LED bulb to reduce eye strain. A floor lamp in the corner creates warm indirect lighting.

## Smart Storage - Keep the Desk Tidy

**Rule: 80% of items stored away, 20% on the desk.** Scandinavian-style filing cabinets typically have flat doors in white or gray, blending into the wall. Open shelving holds only favorite books and a few small decorative items like plants or family photos. Cable management should be hidden in cable ducts or under the desk.

## Inspiration from Nature

**Plants on the desk** are not just decorative but also help reduce stress. Small succulents, mini money trees, or small snake plants in white ceramic pots are popular choices. A Scandinavian landscape painting or botanical print on the wall provides inspiration. On the desk, only keep **a small photo frame, a beautiful notebook, and a quality pen** — enough to show personality.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Japanese Bathroom - The Bathing Ritual and Art of Relaxation
description: Design a bathroom following Japanese philosophy: pure space, natural wood, and traditional onsen bathing rituals.
content:
In Japanese culture, bathing is not merely personal hygiene but a ritual of spiritual purification. The Japanese bathroom (ofuro) is designed as a meditation space where you wash away the troubles of the day. This philosophy can be adapted for Vietnamese bathrooms with appropriate adjustments.

## Separate Washing and Soaking Areas

Unlike Western bathrooms that typically combine shower and toilet in one area, **Japanese bathrooms have clear separation: a standing shower area and a bathing area**. Cleaning the body before entering the soaking tub is an absolute rule. If space allows, design a separate shower stall with a low Japanese-style showerhead and a small wooden sitting stool.

## Wood Materials in the Japanese Bathroom

**Teak wood is the top choice** for Japanese bathrooms in Vietnam thanks to its natural water resistance and termite resistance. Teak shower stools, teak bath mats, and teak wooden ofuro bathtubs are signature items. A teak bathtub retains heat better than ceramic tubs and creates a more natural feeling. For small spaces, at least have **a teak bath mat** under your feet.

## Purifying Colors and Lighting

The Japanese bathroom palette revolves around **deep, dark, and natural** tones: slate, dark wood, and cream white. Walls and floors use **dark gray-black tiles or natural stone** for a hot spring feeling. Lighting should be soft and indirect: recessed LED warm light (2700-3000K), backlit mirror lighting for diffused illumination. Scented candles or eucalyptus/lavender essential oils on wooden shelves enhance the relaxation experience.

## Zen Elements in the Bathroom

**A small zen corner in the bathroom** with a bonsai plant, a bowl of ice stones, or a calligraphy scroll on the wall. A Japanese ceramic vase (tokoname) for flowers or display. A small dish with essential oil and a few pebbles on a wooden shelf. These small details make a big difference.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Modern Minimalist Bathroom - Luxury from Pure Simplicity
description: Create a minimalist bathroom with clean lines, seamless surfaces, and premium materials.
content:
The modern minimalist bathroom is one of today's most beloved interior design trends. With clean lines, seamless surfaces, and emphasis on material quality over quantity of items, a minimalist bathroom delivers an elegant, timeless beauty.

## Seamless Surfaces - The Key Element

**As few grout lines as possible.** Use large tiles (60x60cm or 120x60cm), ideally **large-format stone-look tiles** for both walls and floors to create a seamless effect. Grout color matching the tile helps blur the joints. The bathroom floor should have a gentle slope toward the drain without needing large grout separations. A vessel sink or solid surface sink cast integrated with the countertop is the top choice.

## Wall-Mounted Fixtures

**Wall-hung toilets** and **wall-mounted vanities** keep the floor space open, easy to clean, and create a light feeling. A freestanding bathtub with minimalist geometry — pure rectangle or smooth oval — placed in the center of the bathroom as the focal point. Wall-mounted shower fixtures with a rain shower head hide all plumbing completely in the wall.

## Monochrome Palette

**A minimalist bathroom uses only 2-3 main colors:** white, gray, black, or beige. A pure white bathroom with black accents from faucets, handles, and mirror frames is the icon of minimalism. Or a dark bathroom (charcoal/slate black) with a white tub creates strong contrast. **Avoid using contrasting color blocks or patterns** — uniformity is key.

## Lighting and Mirrors - Expanding the Space

A **frameless mirror** covering the entire wall above the vanity creates a double-space effect. LED strips around the mirror (backlit mirror) provide soft, shadow-free lighting while creating an architectural accent. Combine with recessed downlights and one minimalist pendant light above the bathtub.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Tuscan Style - Italian Countryside Beauty in Vietnamese Homes
description: Explore Tuscan style with warm earth tones, natural materials, and cozy spaces, easily applied in Vietnamese homes.
content:
Tuscan style draws inspiration from the countryside of Tuscany, Italy - known as the 'heart of Italy'. With its warm earthy tones, rustic natural materials, and inviting atmosphere, this style is gaining popularity in Vietnam due to its suitability for tropical climates and alignment with Asian family values.

## Earth Tones - The Soul of Tuscan

The Tuscan palette revolves around fired earth colors: **terracotta, ochre, sienna, and olive green**. Walls are typically painted warm cream or light earth tones, creating a cozy foundation. **Exposed wooden beams** on ceilings, painted dark brown or left in natural wood color, are an indispensable feature.

## Natural and Rustic Materials

**Natural stone, terracotta tiles, and distressed wood** are the three core materials. Floors are laid with terracotta or limestone with slightly rough surfaces, comfortable for barefoot walking. A granite or stacked stone accent wall creates strong architectural impact. Oak or pine with distressed finishes are used for tables, shelves, and door frames.

## Wrought Iron and Handcrafted Items

**Wrought iron chandeliers** with LED candles or Edison bulbs are the hallmark of a Tuscan living room. Large wooden tables with sturdy bases, chairs upholstered in leather or earth-toned linen. Walls display **copper pots, hand-painted ceramic plates, or Italian countryside paintings**. An antique wooden clock or wrought iron mirror frame are perfect accents.

## Warm Lighting

Lighting in Tuscan style must be **warm yellow (2700-3000K)**. Chandeliers, wrought iron sconces, and scented candles on tables create a romantic atmosphere. Large windows with sheer linen curtains allow natural light to highlight the warm tones of the space.

## Applying Tuscan in Vietnam

To apply Tuscan style in Vietnamese homes, consider:
- **Replace fireplaces** (unsuitable for tropical climate) with stone accent walls.
- **Use teak instead of oak** for better humidity resistance.
- **Combine with tropical plants** like olive trees, banyan, or snake plants in terracotta pots.
- **Terracotta bricks** can be replaced with ceramic terracotta-look tiles for easier maintenance.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Remove the TV, Reclaim Your Space - The De-Living-Room Trend
description: 4 de-living-room techniques to spend 80% of the budget and get 120% comfort.
content:
The 'de-living-room' design trend is becoming one of the most talked-about interior design trends of 2026. Instead of the traditional living room with a sofa facing a TV, this trend proposes a more flexible open space that serves multiple real-life purposes.

## What is De-Living-Room Design?

'De-living-room' does not mean having no living room at all. Rather, it is about **breaking the fixed layout** of the traditional living room — sofa + coffee table + TV — and redesigning the space according to your family's actual needs. It could become a library, a yoga studio, a children's play area, or a home office.

## Technique 1: Modular Furniture

Instead of a large fixed sofa set, use **modular seating that can be moved and rearranged** as needed. When you need more space, the seats can be tucked into a corner. When guests arrive, they can be pulled out to form a conversation area. Floor seating with cushions and throw pillows is also a flexible and space-saving option.

## Technique 2: Multi-Functional Zones

One open space can serve multiple purposes: **a reading + work area**, a dining + entertainment area, or a children's play + adult relaxation area. The key is using **area rugs** and **multi-purpose tables** to divide zones without needing walls.

## Technique 3: Light Zoning

Instead of building walls, use **lighting to divide the space**. Pendant lights over the dining area, floor lamps in the reading corner, and LED strip lights on the ceiling for the shared space. Each zone has a different color temperature and brightness level, creating natural visual boundaries.

## Technique 4: Dynamic Partitions

Use **movable partitions, curtains, or open bookshelves** instead of fixed walls. Partitions can be opened when you need a wide space and closed when you need privacy. Open bookshelves serve as both partitions and display space — beautiful and practical.

## Practical Benefits

- **Save 20-30% on furniture costs** because you don't need a large sofa set and TV.
- **Increase usable area by 30-50%** thanks to multi-functional space design.
- **Ideal for small homes** from 50-80 square meters.
- **Boost family interaction** since the TV is no longer the center of attention.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: French Style Secrets - 99% of People Make These Mistakes
description: 8 essential elements for proper French style decoration, avoiding the most common pitfalls.
content:
French style has always been the dream of many families. However, 90% of homes marketed as 'French style' make serious mistakes. French style is not just about applying a few crown moldings and hanging a chandelier — it requires mastering **8 essential elements**.

## Mistake 1: Overuse of Crown Molding

Many people think that more crown molding equals more 'French'. In reality, too many moldings on walls and ceilings create a cluttered, cramped feeling rather than elegance. **Principle: less is more.** You only need 2-3 refined moldings in strategic positions: ceiling edge, door frame, and possibly an arch molding on the wall.

## Mistake 2: Wrong Chandelier Proportions

A chandelier too small for a large room looks out of place, while one too large for a small room overwhelms the space. **Rule: the chandelier diameter should be 1/3 to 1/2 the room width.** Hang the chandelier 75-90cm above the table surface.

## Mistake 3: Wrong Color Palette

French style uses a **warm color palette**: cream, beige, light turquoise, earth yellow, and warm white. Avoid pure white (cool white) or cold gray — these belong to modern style, not French.

## Mistake 4: Style Mixing Mistakes

Don't mix modern minimalist furniture (black leather sofa, glass table) with French decoration. **Tufted upholstered beds, curved sofas with cabriole legs, and slim-legged round tables** — that is what real French furniture looks like.

## Mistake 5: Cheap Materials

Faux marble artificial stone, thin and fragile crown moldings, acrylic chandeliers — all of these create a 'fake' and cheap feeling. **Invest in real materials:** genuine marble, crown moldings at least 5cm thick, crystal or brass chandeliers.

## Mistake 6: Neglecting Details

French style lies in the **details**: brass door handles, gold picture frames, scented candles on the table, linen curtains that touch the floor. These small details make the difference between 'real French' and 'fake French'.

## Mistake 7: Wrong Lighting

French style requires **warm yellow light (2700-3000K)**. Cold white 6500K LED lights will completely destroy the French atmosphere. Use chandeliers, wall sconces, and candles to create layered lighting.

## Mistake 8: Missing Focal Point

Every French room needs **one strong focal point**: a large gold-framed mirror, a large painting, or an impressive chandelier. Without a focal point, the space will feel empty and lack character.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: Luxury on a Budget - 9 Low-Cost Ways to Create a Premium Home
description: 9 practical methods to achieve a luxurious look without breaking the bank.
content:
Many people think that a luxurious space requires a large budget. In reality, with the **9 simple methods** below, you can absolutely create a high-quality home without spending too much.

## 1. Unified Wall-Ceiling-Floor Color Scheme

Inconsistent colors are the main reason a space looks cheap. **Choose a warm earth-tone palette** (beige, cream, light brown) and apply it consistently to walls, ceilings, and floors. This creates a seamless, spacious, and luxurious feel. The number of interior colors should not exceed 3 tones.

## 2. No-Main-Light Design

Instead of one large chandelier in the center of the room, use **recessed ceiling lights, wall sconces, and floor lamps** distributed evenly. Layered lighting creates depth and a luxurious atmosphere. If your budget is limited, prioritize lighting for the living room and master bedroom.

## 3. Light on Hard Decor, Heavy on Soft Decor

Don't invest too much in complex ceilings or granite walls. Instead, **keep ceilings and walls simple**, and invest in quality curtains, area rugs, throw pillows, and sofa throws. These soft furnishings make direct contact with the body and instantly create a sense of luxury.

## 4. Negative Space

Don't fill every corner of the room. **Negative space is a sign of design confidence.** A white wall with a single painting, a corner with just one chair and a plant — these empty areas create breathing room and an elegant feel.

## 5. Pay Attention to Hardware

Door handles, hinges, faucets, towel racks — these small details are touched every day. **Invest in brass or matte black hardware** with refined lines. Simply replacing all the door handles in your home will surprise you with the difference it makes.

## 6. Choose Meaningful Artwork

A single large, meaningful painting on a white wall can elevate an entire room. **Don't buy cheap decorative art from supermarkets.** Choose a piece you truly love — it could be a photo from a trip, or a large-format art print. A simple wood or metal frame will complete the look.

## 7. Statement Plants

Instead of many small, cheap potted plants, choose **1-2 large plants with beautiful shapes** such as a fiddle-leaf fig, monstera, or olive tree. Place them in simple ceramic pots. Large plants create spatial depth and a sense of connection with nature.

## 8. Forget Style Labels

Don't try to force your home into a 'minimalist' or 'French' label. Instead, **focus on living logic**: what you need, what you like, and how you use the space. A home designed around real-life logic will naturally be beautiful and luxurious.

## 9. Make the Most of Natural Light

Natural light is the best free decorating material. **Sheer white-cream curtains**, large unobstructed windows, and mirrors placed opposite windows to reflect light — all of these cost nothing but create astonishingly luxurious results.
author: NhàXinh Editorial

title: 7 Kitchen Details Most Likely to Fail - Avoid Before It's Too Late
description: Common kitchen design mistakes and how to fix them.
content:
The kitchen is the most frequently used room in the home, but also the place where design mistakes are most likely to happen. Here are the **7 kitchen details most likely to 'fail'**, according to experts.

## 1. Matte Tiles, Trending Tiles, Subway Tiles

Matte tiles on kitchen walls are very difficult to clean of grease. Trending tiles and subway tiles have too many grout lines — each line is a place where grease and mold accumulate. **Solution:** Use glossy or semi-gloss tiles in light colors, with large sizes (30x60cm or larger) to reduce grout lines.

## 2. Choosing the Wrong Grout/Caulking

Regular white grout will turn yellow after just a few months of use. Epoxy grout is durable but prone to peeling when the base is not flat. **Solution:** Use waterproof, stain-resistant grout (epoxy or polyaspartic) in light gray or beige — these colors hide dirt better than pure white.

## 3. Thin Sintered Stone Countertops

Ultra-thin sintered stone countertops look beautiful but chip very easily at the edges. When chopping food, the clanging sound is annoying. **Solution:** Choose quartz stone 20-30mm thick, or solid surface material. Thicker but much more durable, and won't make noise when cutting.

## 4. Integrated Cooker (Range Hood + Stove Combo)

An integrated cooker looks neat and tidy, but when one part breaks, you have to replace the entire unit. Repair costs are high, and replacement options are limited. **Solution:** Buy the stove and range hood separately. Easier to replace, easier to repair, and more choices available.

## 5. Double-Basin Sink Instead of a Large Single Basin

A double-basin sink looks convenient, but each basin is too small — you can't fit large pots or pans. **Solution:** Choose a large single basin sink with minimum dimensions of 60x45cm. Washing pots and pans is effortless, and you can use a divider tray when needed.

## 6. Ceiling Fan Cooler in the Kitchen

A ceiling fan cooler in the kitchen blows hot air down onto the person cooking — making it even hotter. The cooling effect is practically zero. **Solution:** Install a mini air conditioner, or draw cool air from another room. If budget is limited, open the window and use a standing fan blowing horizontally.

## 7. Top-Hung Sliding Door

A top-hung sliding door looks elegant, but the rollers break easily, the heavy door panel warps, and maintenance is difficult. After 1-2 years, the door usually squeaks or doesn't slide smoothly. **Solution:** Choose a bottom-track sliding door or a traditional swing door. More durable, easier to repair, and better sealed — effectively blocking cooking odors from spreading to the living room.
author: NhàXinh Editorial
